q: A poison blocks the enzyme that oxidises triose phosphate in glycolysis. What happens to the ATP balance of glycolysis?
options: Net yield stays at 2 ATP, because all of the ATP is formed during the phosphorylation stage
Net yield rises to 4 ATP, because no ATP is needed to oxidise the triose phosphate
Glycolysis now uses 2 ATP per glucose but makes none, as ATP-forming steps come later
Only the yield of reduced NAD is affected; the ATP output of glycolysis stays exactly the same
explanation: Glycolysis 'invests' 2 ATP early (phosphorylating glucose). The 'payoff' – oxidation of triose phosphate (reducing NAD+) followed by 4 ATP from substrate-level phosphorylation – comes only after lysis. Blocking the oxidation step stops the payoff, so each glucose costs 2 ATP and triose phosphate accumulates.
